04 / UNDERSTAND

Know the reason behind the route.

This is graph-search AI: explicit algorithms choose the next state to explore. No trained model, live traffic feed or chatbot is required.

Your 30-second project explanation

“PathMind models a map as a weighted graph. Each walkable cell is a node, and four-direction moves are edges. I implemented five search algorithms and compare their explored nodes, steps, weighted cost and runtime. A* uses Manhattan distance to guide its search; Dijkstra uses accumulated cost. BFS optimizes steps on equal-cost graphs, while DFS and Greedy do not guarantee a minimum-cost route.”

Try this in your demo

  1. Select The weighted shortcut and run a comparison.
  2. Show how BFS and Greedy cross expensive cells while A* and Dijkstra find a cheaper detour.
  3. Choose No route challenge to demonstrate a correctly detected failure.
  4. Step through A* and explain g(n), h(n), and f(n).

Scope and assumptions

Simulated grid, not a real street map. Move costs are 1 or 5; walls are impassable. Start cost is excluded. Movement is four-directional with no diagonals. Ties use insertion order (neighbors: up, right, down, left). DFS pops the most recently added neighbor. All searches use O(V) auxiliary space on this bounded-degree grid. Random maps are not guaranteed to be connected.
